chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Salim, from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr, from Husayn ibn Abdullah, from his father, from his grandfather, who said:
Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'When a man has multiple horses during a military expedition, a share is allocated to him for only two of them.'

key_terms.أَفْرَاسٌ: Plural of horse, referring to cavalry mounts
key_terms.يُسْهَمْ: Passive verb meaning 'a share is allocated/distributed'

ai.seo_question: What is the limit on horse shares in Islamic war booty distribution?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the specific limit of two horse shares per soldier in ghanimah distribution, reflecting the early Islamic military structure where cavalry was a premium asset. It underscores the principle of equitable resource allocation by preventing the accumulation of excessive wealth from a single combatant's multiple mounts, a ruling consistent with the practices of Imam Ali (AS) during the Rashidun era. The limitation highlights the distinction between personal property and state-allocated military resources in Shia jurisprudence.

en.hubeali: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Salim, from Ahmad Bin Al Nazar, from Husayn Bin Abdullah, from his father, from his grandfather who said,
‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘When there were (many) horses for the man during a military expedition, there would not be distributed to him except for the two horses from these’.
en.sarwar: 3. Abu Ali al-Ash’ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn Salim from Ahmad ibn al-Al-Nadr ibn al-Suwayd from al-Husayn ibn ‘Abd Allah from his father from his grandfather who has said the following:
“If a person had many horses during a war Amir al-Mu’minin, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, would give him the shares for two of his horses only.”
